title: Cube-Difference Factor Absorbing Primary Ideals of Commutative Rings
content: Let R be a commutative ring with nonzero identity. A proper ideal I of R is cube-difference factor absorbing primary (cdf-primary) if, for all a, b ∈R, a3−b3 ∈ I implies a−b ∈ I or a2 + ab+ b2 ∈ √I. This is the cubic counterpart of square-differencefactor absorbing primarity, and it lies strictly between the cdf-absorbing and the cdf-semiprimary conditions. A recurring theme throughout is the protective role played bythe prime 3, which has no counterpart in the quadratic theory and already separatesthe two conditions at the level of Z: the ideal 21Z is cdf-primary while the sdf-primaryideal 14Z is not. For a radical ideal with finitely many pairwise comaximal minimalprimes we characterize cdf-primarity completely: at most one of the residue domainsmay have a fraction field containing a primitive cube root of unity, and then the resthave characteristic 3. The same criterion governs the radical ideals of a ZPI-ring. Over Z, for n ≥ 2 the ideal nZ is cdf-primary exactly when n is a prime power, or n = 3pk with p ̸= 3 prime, or n is squarefree with no prime factor congruent to 1 modulo 3.We also treat a weak variant and the behavior of cdf-primarity under the standard ringconstructions.
